name: WPGrock Appointment Booking
author: wpgrock

sections.description:
WPGrock Appointment Booking is a free WordPress appointment scheduling plugin for service businesses that want customers to book appointments through a simple online calendar.

Display available dates and time slots, collect customer details through a booking form, and manage appointments from your WordPress dashboard. Configure weekly working hours, breaks, blackout dates, service durations, and booking timezones.

Features

  • Monday-to-Sunday front-end calendar.
  • Monday-to-Sunday admin appointment calendar.
  • Current date selected automatically on the front end.
  • First active service loaded by default.
  • Optional service selector when no service is specified in the shortcode.
  • Service-specific shortcode support: [wpgrock_booking service=”Service Name”].
  • Service shortcode mode hides the service selector and loads the requested service only.
  • Service management with name, description, duration, buffer time and active/inactive status.
  • No currency or payment fields in the free version.
  • Pricing or other information can be included in the service description.
  • Weekly availability with up to two working ranges per day.
  • 24-hour time inputs for split working hours or lunch breaks.
  • Blackout dates and date ranges.
  • Calendar-based available slot generation.
  • Popup lead/customer form after a time slot is selected.
  • Appointment confirmation shown inside the booking popup.
  • Server-side slot validation.
  • Concurrent booking protection and double-booking prevention.
  • Appointment statuses including pending, confirmed, completed, cancelled and no-show.
  • Separate admin Calendar View and List View for appointments.
  • Appointment list filters for All, Upcoming and Recent appointments.
  • Recent appointments are displayed in descending date/time order.
  • Appointment export as Excel-compatible CSV.
  • Dashboard sections for today’s appointments, active services and recent customer appointments.
  • Customer management.
  • Email notifications using WordPress wp_mail().
  • Configurable booking timezone using named timezone identifiers.
  • Timezone is displayed to customers on the booking calendar.
  • Responsive front-end booking interface.
  • Styling settings for text, buttons, selected dates, normal dates and unavailable dates.
  • AJAX booking and availability.
  • Gutenberg appointment booking block.
  • REST API endpoints.
  • WordPress privacy exporter and eraser callbacks.
  • Translation-ready strings.
  • Separate SQL tables created during plugin activation.
  • Optional data erasure when the plugin is deleted.

Privacy

WPGrock Appointment Booking stores customer name, email, phone, appointment information and optional booking messages submitted through the site. This information is stored locally in the WordPress database and is used to manage appointments and send booking notifications. The plugin does not transmit customer data to external services by default. Site administrators should configure their privacy policy and data retention practices for their specific business and jurisdiction.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the WPGrock Appointment Booking folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate WPGrock Appointment Booking. Its custom database tables are created during activation.
  3. Go to WPGrock Appointment Booking > Services and create at least one active service.
  4. Go to WPGrock Appointment Booking > Availability and configure one or two working ranges for each day.
  5. Optionally add WPGrock Appointment Booking > Blackout Dates.
  6. Check WPGrock Appointment Booking > Settings and choose the booking timezone for the business.
  7. Add [wpgrock_booking] to a page, or use [wpgrock_booking service=”Your Service Name”] to load one service without a service selector.
  8. Configure front-end colors under WPGrock Appointment Booking > Styling.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Renamed the plugin to WPGrock Appointment Booking and aligned the package slug, text domain and WordPress.org contributor identity.
  • Fixed the activation database setup by correctly declaring the WordPress database object before reading its charset/collation.
  • Updated the Gutenberg block namespace and metadata to the new plugin identity.
  • Updated documentation and visible plugin branding for the new name.
  • Kept the existing appointment-booking feature set and security/privacy controls.

1.3.4

  • Removed the Tested up to header from the main plugin file; it is maintained only in readme.txt.
  • Updated the plugin text domain to match the WordPress.org slug.

1.3.2

  • Fixed Plugin Check internationalization, nonce, SQL preparation, and filesystem warnings.

1.3.0

  • Standardized front-end and admin calendars to Monday through Sunday.
  • Moved appointment confirmation into the booking popup.
  • Added first-active-service default behavior.
  • Added service-name shortcode locking.
  • Added All, Upcoming and Recent appointment filters.
  • Added dashboard detail sections for appointments, services and recent customers.
  • Added configurable named booking timezone with daylight-saving support.
  • Improved two-range availability editing and loading.

1.2.0

  • Added calendar-first booking UI, popup lead form, styling and split working hours.

1.1.0

  • Added calendar-first front-end booking UI and admin calendar/list views.

1.0.0

  • Initial free MVP.
